findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses AND, so neither role alone can add guests
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...). A user who is only a team admin, or only a team owner, fails both this flag and the organizer/attendee checks and gets FORBIDDEN. The name and the usual Cal.com permission model require OR. teamId ?? 0 also runs those checks against team 0 for personal event types, which cannot succeed. Team admins/owners therefore cannot add guests to team bookings unless they are also the booking user or an attendee.

findings.title: Calendar attendee update uses the actor's credentials, not the organizer's
findings.body: getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and EventManager are built from the logged-in caller, while booking.user.credentials (already loaded) is ignored. updateCalendarAttendees then runs as whoever clicked Add. When a team admin or attendee adds guests, the organizer's Google/Outlook event is not updated (or the call fails), so new guests never appear on the host calendar even though they were written to the booking.

findings.title: Emails are keyed off the raw guest list, not the guests actually inserted
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) receives the original input, not uniqueGuests. The mailer treats any address in that list as a brand-new invitee and sends AttendeeScheduledEmail (full confirmation, ICS REQUEST, meeting link) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Re-submitting an existing attendee's address therefore sends them another booking confirmation, and blacklisted addresses that were filtered out of the DB write can still be treated as new guests if they were already on the booking.

findings.title: Duplicate and blacklist checks are case-sensitive
findings.body: uniqueGuests compares guest === attendee.email and blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing only the env list. Zod's email() does not normalize case, so Guest@x.com is inserted again when guest@x.com is already an attendee, and a blacklisted address is accepted if the casing differs. That creates duplicate attendee rows and bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.

findings.title: No booking status, time, or seat-capacity checks before adding guests
findings.body: The handler updates any booking by id once the caller passes the permission check. Cancelled, rejected, and past bookings still get new attendee rows and confirmation emails with the meeting link. Seated event types (seatsPerTimeSlot) are not checked, so createMany can push attendance past the seat limit and treat extra people as full attendees rather than seats. There is also no guard that the event type allows additional guests.

findings.title: Add-guest emails ignore event-type email disable flags
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails always emails the organizer, every team member, and every attendee. Unlike sendScheduledEmails and sendLocationChangeEmails, it never consults disableStandardEmails for host or attendee. Event types that turned standard emails off still blast guest-added mail and full scheduled emails (with ICS and video links) to every new address.

findings.title: Custom email title and subject are overridden by spread props
findings.body: Both AttendeeAddGuestsEmail and OrganizerAddGuestsEmail set title, subject, and headerType, then spread {...props} afterward. Component props that include those fields replace the guest-specific copy, so the React email renders as a normal scheduled email (and OrganizerAddGuestsEmail's callToAction={null} is likewise overwritten). The nodemailer subject can still be correct, but the HTML body title/CTA will not match the 'guests added' intent whenever those props are passed through renderEmail.
